case_selection.why: the smallest set that uses only reviewed behaviour: the ten faculty-reviewed paths are all of gi_bleed_57m, and in that one case the course itself gives both pilot situations -- volume and blood with reassessment, and a pressure that falls again so that norepinephrine at an explicit rate becomes a decision; gi_bleed_72f runs under the same authority but was not part of the human management-trace review, so it is DEFERRED

fail_safe.behaviour: the encounter stops (AUTHORITY_STOP); no fallback to the earlier model; the record keeps everything up to the stop

fail_safe.situation: no authority site for a pilot encounter

fail_safe.behaviour: recorded as not understood, or held for the reader's question; nothing is done; the encounter goes on
fail_safe.situation: unrecognized or incomplete order BEFORE the first committed minute

fail_safe.behaviour: the development experiment stops permanently (the certified authority rule MINUTE_ALREADY_COMMITTED, P3-28; found again by the pilot dry run, unchanged here); the encounter ends with the operational message. This is fail closed, and it is the pilot's main open readiness problem (TD-165)
fail_safe.situation: a turn that does not move the clock AFTER the first committed minute and is not purely structural (an incomplete order the reader must ask about, an order it does not understand, a target instead of a rate, a question typed as an order)

fail_safe.behaviour: the development experiment stops (AUTHORITY_STOP, the certified fail-closed behaviour, unchanged); the encounter ends with the operational message; nothing is invented
fail_safe.situation: an order the engine carries out but the development authority does not represent (e.g. tranexamic acid, analgesia, other medications)

fail_safe.behaviour: the reader asks for an explicit rate with its unit (the approved text); nothing is carried out

fail_safe.behaviour: the encounter ends at once at the development boundary; what followed is not shown

fail_safe.behaviour: the encounter ends at the development boundary
the encounter stops; nothing more is carried out (fails closed)
fail_safe.situation: pilot record unavailable or its faculty log broken

fail_safe.behaviour: the participant's trace is withheld; the faculty sees MISMATCH and the encounter is not usable for analysis
the encounter ends at the faculty stop on the participant's next action or refresh

fail_safe.situation: UI refresh, new tab or process restart

fail_safe.behaviour: the open one is recorded INTERRUPTED before the new one starts, and on its own next run it ends (ENCOUNTER_CLOSED_IN_RECORD): it never continues, so no participant runs two encounters
fail_safe.situation: a second encounter started while one is open (another tab of the same participant)

fail_safe.behaviour: appends are serialized and locked, so the chain never forks; the write check is unique per call
fail_safe.situation: two sessions writing the pilot record at the same moment
